chunk_findings.detail: `chat_t3` only returns true when `cfg.sources.get("approvals.accept_chat_for_t3") == "local"`. The operator decision D-RA-T3-chat only requires the opt-in to be on; it does not say the opt-in is limited to `.ddflow/local/config.toml`, and the config system demonstrably supports environment-delivered approval knobs (`DDFLOW_APPROVALS_FORBID_CHAT_FOR_T3` is checked in `_forbidden`). Given `DDFLOW_APPROVALS_ACCEPT_CHAT_FOR_T3=true` with no local file, `cfg.approvals.accept_chat_for_t3` is true but the source is not `"local"`, so `chat_t3` returns False and a typed T3 attestation that D-RA-T3-chat says should be accepted is rejected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:chat_t3

chunk_findings.detail: When `_gate_problem(prev, text)` is falsy, the new operand constructs `KeyRefused(AG.problem(_parsed(prev), _parsed(text)))` unconditionally. For an edit with no approvals problem, `AG.problem(...)` returns `None`, so this expression evaluates to a truthy `KeyRefused(None)` instance (Python objects are truthy unless a custom `__bool__` is defined, and this change does not add one). The surrounding `or` therefore returns that empty refusal object immediately, making the later `_human_removed` and `_workflow_refusal` checks unreachable. Input: a config edit that needs a workflow/human-removed refusal but has no approvals guard problem; line 809 stops before those guards and refuses the edit with no message.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:809 KeyRefused(AG.problem(...))

chunk_findings.detail: `new = 'false'` is the TOML string `"false"`, not the boolean `false` (which must be written without quotes). The key `approvals.forbid_chat_for_t3` is a boolean config option whose default is meant to be off. When this `knob_added` record is folded into a release and consumed by the upgrade/configwrite path, it carries a string where a bool is required: either the config parser rejects the wrong type, or a non-empty string `"false"` is truthy and the default becomes effectively “forbid on,” silently forbidding all typed T3 chat.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.approvals.forbid_chat_for_t3.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The autouse fixture clears only `DDFLOW_AGENT` and `AP.HARNESS_MARKERS`, but does not clear the new approval-knob environment variables. A test process with `DDFLOW_APPROVALS_FORBID_CHAT_FOR_T3=true` exported (the same variable `test_the_environment_can_forbid` relies on) will make `test_a_typed_answer_approves_a_t3_act_and_is_graded` fail: `_cfg` creates a config with `forbid_chat_for_t3=False`, but `H.attest`/`H.chat_t3` sees the environment's forbid and refuses the approval, so the test's `assert ok, message` fails. The fixture should clear `DDFLOW_APPROVALS_FORBID_CHAT_FOR_T3` (and `DDFLOW_APPROVALS_ACCEPT_CHAT_FOR_T3`) to make the tests hermetic.

chunk_findings.detail: `except FileNotFoundError: continue` is meant to skip only an absent layer, but `os.stat(path)` also raises `FileNotFoundError` for a broken symlink at a layer path (the symlink entry exists, but its target is missing). That broken/unreadable layer is silently skipped, so `_forbidden` returns `False` and `chat_t3` can become `True` even though an existing layer path could not be read. This contradicts the code's own fail-closed rule that an unreadable existing layer may be the one that forbids. Input: point a lower-precedence layer such as `.ddflow/local/config.toml` at a nonexistent target; `os.stat` raises `FileNotFoundError`, the branch continues, and the layer is not treated as forbidden.
